content: Huginn TUI confirm bar ends with `? Enter yes · Esc no`, and the edit prompt names the editor, e.g. `Edit <id> in subl --wait?`.
Huginn CLI has `ls`, `next`, `show <id>`, and `tui` (interactive list and board); there is no non-interactive board command yet.
Proposed by the agent, not yet accepted: huginn lint flags a nonexistent parent, a parent cycle, and a done epic with open children.
muninn config setting `"embedder"` accepts builtin|ollama|none; `muninn model status` shows which is in use; `muninn serve` keeps the model loaded (~30-40 ms recall vs ~0.19 s without).
Hug TUI reloads are deferred while a prompt, confirm, palette or editor is open, and selection is tracked by task id so a rename elsewhere keeps it.
Default proposal for project memories is branch `muninn-notes` mounted at `.muninn-notes/`, since `.muninn/` already holds marker files.
User prefers recall blocks to state rules as a plain sentence rather than as SDD properties, since property-form rules get misread as data.
Hug recall board nudge: inject at most one board line per session hour, only on a detected mismatch, with the exact command to run (hug task take ID, hug task done ID, hug task check ID N).
Hug worker protocol: the worker name is the middle part of $JCODE_SESSION_ID, and `hug task take` is called with `--as <name> --model claude-opus-5-5`.
`hug mem forget` runs a full index pass before and after, each inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; with ~120 parallel forgets, waiters exceed the 30s busy_timeout and fail with SQLITE_BUSY.
Offline hug output reports `sync: N unpushed` with `fix: hug task sync`, and catches up when the remote is back.
`hug task ls` prints ticked/total as the fourth field after the type, keeping the id as field 1 for script compatibility.
muninn's repo remote uses SSH because the gh token lacks the `workflow` scope, so workflow files must be pushed over SSH.
hug's markdown renderer (glamour) drops `<dir>`-style text as raw HTML; the fix backslash-escapes `<` outside code spans/fences before rendering.
muninn fix 7bdb2e9 (v0.4.0-10) raises whole-run capture limit to 180s (per-call 45s, max 15 min) to stop timeouts under load.
Learned 'not when' recall needs relevance signals from daily use (memory_feedback, forgets, dream vetting), which do not exist yet.

Board nudge design: one extra line in the recall block after ranking (like the dream cue), recall ranking unchanged; fires on editing-with-no-task, all-checks-ticked, working on a todo task, and lint; at most one board line per session hour; nudge_board=false disables it.
hug CLI accepts `task:<id>` refs everywhere: a helper strips the leading `task:` in Resolve/ResolveDependency, and printed commands echo the bare id.
User wants the next work framed as their own locally-optimized memory system (not called observational memory), built as a new objective.
hug TUI reload design (Jørgen's ruling): nothing reloads automatically; when a newer hug appears at the start path only the version corner changes, and R reloads.
jhf approved building project identity and JSONL sync for muninn at 15:40.
Repository export stays strict on secrets (the branch's secret gate would refuse such lines), even though recall/display no longer redact.
huginn release tooling mirrors muninn's: build-release.sh, package-managers.sh, install.sh, release.yml; 6 platforms CGO off, SHA256SUMS, TAP_DEPLOY_KEY secret for the shared homebrew-tap.
User wants muninn recall output to include a small amount of ASCII formatting (e.g. a framed block) to help agents read it.
muninn: memories should get short ticket-style ids, with a separate mapping table for import origin instead of long prefixed names; also compact memories.
In hug, a "Depends on" line only counts as a dependency if it looks like `- <id>`; other prose gets a `not-a-dependency` finding and creates no dependency.
A hug note costs about 440 ms on this machine with or without background sync, so the 'under 400 ms' target for a note cannot be met by any note.
Hug worker protocol: the final report lists commits, the verbatim last test line, the cause of the SQLITE_BUSY, and open questions, and is also written to tmp/lanes/me51r2.md.
Huginn TUI key bindings: n/p step between tasks and N creates a task; following a dependency, Esc back and n/p all reset focus to the task's starting point.
muninn recall takes 110-180 ms with Ollama's embedding model loaded; first call after unload takes 420-650 ms.
Muninn configuration lives in a `config` subdirectory under MUNINN_HOME; tests must create it.

Muninn recall tuning issue: worker status/completion messages trigger irrelevant recall matches on generic ops words (deploy, verified, main, worktree); suggested fix is to skip recall for worker messages or raise the score threshold.

User wants a client-scoped mode: a marker directory (user suggested `.muninn/client` file) makes its folder a client root; inside it agents see only that client's memories, and nothing outside can see them.
hug task set has no --model flag, so a task reassigned via set records the assignee but not the model.
Board nudge replay must filter by working directory: animal session names are reused across repos, so the hug board was wrongly applied to older sessions from other repos.
Hug TUI goldens are regenerated with `HUGINN_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 GOMAXPROCS=2 nice -n 19 go test -run TestTmuxGolden ./huginn/internal/tui/`, then the diff is reviewed for intended changes.
huginn's backlog importer ignored `parent_task_id`, so seid's 190 parent links were lost on import; the importer needs to resolve parents through aliases and stay idempotent on re-run.
muninn is public at https://github.com/veridit/muninn (MPL-2.0, latest release v0.1.2), a single Go program for 6 platforms built only from seid search code, nothing from jcode.
hug memory conditions (--holds) accept "until DATE", "while task:ID open" and "while branch NAME unmerged"; when a condition ends recall hides the memory and dream offers it once, nothing is deleted.
muninn's MCP server is stdio only, there is no versioned migration system yet, and the background service does not use a socket.
In hug, commit paths are relative to the worktree (r.Dir) and task paths are relative to the store root, and the two roots are the same.

Muninn scoping is shipped live (v0.3.0-13, installed after a fresh backup): client instances see only their own memories, global memories and the current project; global/Claude Code/Codex see everything except client instances.
Each single hug mem forget still runs a full index pass, so queued forgets on a cold store take 36-66 s each; a batch forget runs one pass.
hug's TUI tests have a load guard that skips running when the machine's 5-minute load average is too high (e.g. over 120).
hug mem writes (remember, forget, rescope, correct, tidy, index) queue on one cross-process lock; nested writes reuse it, recall hooks never wait.
muninn background commands now run niced (nice 10) while interactive commands like search stay at nice 0; installed live as v0.4.0-5-g7612828.
muninn v0.1.2 (2026, veridit/muninn) fixed stale kNN neighbour links, Ollama-outage recall fallback to keyword matching, older /api/embeddings support, and a TUI 'forgot' confirmation glitch.
hug TUI help screen truncates columns at width 140; long palette descriptions widen the navigation column and cut the actions column, so descriptions must stay short.
Hug lint findings must not use the word "dangling" in text a person reads; keep the code `dangling-dependency` for missing-task dependencies.
muninn v0.2.0 publishes installs via GitHub Actions: Homebrew tap veridit/homebrew-tap (needs one-time `brew trust`), Scoop bucket, and a checksum-verifying install.sh.
gitbranch.Open always uses the branch's single checkout in the main worktree (creating it there if absent); the opt-in WithSharedCheckout option was removed.
Evidence should be a generic directory name rather than 'evidence', and references between tasks' evidence should be allowed and validated.
Hug CLI tests used an `ed.sh` shebang script as the editor, which cannot be exec'd on Windows; the test binary acting as the editor is the portable replacement.
muninn recall latency was cut from 0.86-1.9s to 0.17-0.21s at 16.6k memories by keeping a precomputed count table; golden recall check passes 9/9.
muninn now asks "are you sure there are no secrets here?" at write time instead of hiding content at read time.
Recall3 strict confirmation gate requires fresh sessions starting after the freeze (30 messages/8 sessions); as of the report only 2 human messages from 1 new session existed, so the gate is blocked.
hug CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) also runs on pushes to ci/** branches, so CI branches get a run without touching main.
muninn has a `muninn types` command that labels memories by type; it is resumable and supports `--dry-run`.
Crab's rulings: lint ticket x325pp comes after s6ff5k, which comes after ez50rb; seid board latency stays with humpback.
User wants to revisit later how muninn judges whether a memory is personal vs not, and how imported data is handled; both should be added to the to-dos.
hug's git fast path (local config defining `origin`) is the only case where remote resolution cannot depend on global git config; otherwise fall back to asking git.
hug TUI: all closed tasks appear under RECENTLY DONE, each section keeps its own scroll position across Tab, and a None item sits on the title line.
Recall3 constraints: no production changes, no live memory writes, no push to main, no installs, and do not change the frozen configuration.
Worker assignments: tiger tests recall variants, turkey tests capture variants, parrot benchmarks seid-style search speed in Go, squid handles capture batching and releases.

muninn tidy rule (2026-11-07): moves stay within the client a memory was written in; targets must be concrete scopes; ambiguous group-only targets are dropped and counted, never guessed; jcode@global is a target only when most similar neighbors are there.
CHANGELOG.md in hug often holds other agents' uncommitted lines, so commit only your own hunk (e.g. git apply --cached) or work from a clean worktree off origin/main.
hug memory agent-name matching maps each memory to the session of that name that was running when it was written (using updated_ns as write time), since agent names get reused.
muninn's jcode hook is installed in all 6 jcode instances via `muninn install jcode --all-instances`, with per-instance memory isolation verified by jcode-instances-e2e.sh in CI.
User agreed an acceptance item that grows into a task is promoted to a sibling task under the same epic, or standalone if there is no epic, and the item links to it.
User decided every huginn task has a short unique ID (snowflake-like) plus a human-meaningful slug; humans see the slug, everything under the hood uses the ID.
Engram-imported memories are placed by recorded working directory: jcode instance folders → that instance, other git projects → that project, home/non-git/deleted folders → global.

Recall3 verdict is NO SHIP; the frozen comparison remains valid despite today's production recall changes (harness notices skipped, engram memories placed by folder, global binding excluding other projects' project: scopes), which require separate replication.
Attachments/evidence keep a tree structure (folders preserved) rather than flat prefixed filenames.
hug task take records an assignee name and model via Store.TakeAs; Take keeps its signature because the TUI calls it.
Live hook latency gate for board.Open is 50 ms p95; hug board measured 33 ms p95 after optimization, seid 168 ms p95 dominated by cache.Open loading ~2,508 task rows in humpback's package.
In hug, every git network call runs without prompts and has a deadline; a board lock stops a background rebase from moving files under a running command.
hug CLI and MCP both signal an outdated repo layout: task commands and task_next fail with a 'fix: hug upgrade' line, and hug setup lists the upgrade as the first open step.
Short-id migration is live: all 20,744 muninn memories have unique 6-char ids; recall entries render as `- [YYYY-MM-DD id] …`.
hug mem list --json and hug mem search --json print one object of shape {"memories": [...]}.
User wants both memories and tickets to store the original imported source ID so imports are idempotent without reusing source numbering.
Hug workers must not touch huginn/internal/tui/ while another worker edits it; DM the coordinator before touching other shared files.
Hug tests for worktree/board behavior use temp dirs with real git: create a repo, a board, a linked worktree, and assert no extra worktree entry appears in `git worktree list`.
hug's cache is shared, so switching binaries rebuilds it; per-step memory numbers must warm each binary twice before measuring.
hug TUI overview layout: the focused section takes all spare rows; unfocused sections show up to 3 rows, and RECENTLY DONE lists all closed tasks newest first.
huginn is a Go git-branch task tracker (repo veridit/huginn, MPL-2.0, no secrets), sister project of muninn; released publicly at v0.1.0 then v0.1.1.
Muninn capture2 development-only prompt choice was frozen as `langmem` for the exact Flash/Luna/Haiku comparison; all eight development sessions scored and whole-tree replay validation passed.
muninn's Claude Code and Codex hooks output the documented format but are not yet installed or live-tested; opencode has no native plugin, so MCP and `muninn recall` serve any agent.
`hug upgrade` prints nothing in text mode (pre-existing behavior); tests should use `--json` via execute instead.
huginn: build the TUI now; web UI is deferred for both huginn and muninn.
User chose the name "muninn" (Odin's raven, two n's) for the local memory tool, over ai-local-memory, minne and huske.
Hug lint findings carry a `fix` field; `hug task lint` prints `  fix: …` under each finding and `next:` is the first finding's fix (text and --json).
CI on muninn main had been failing since 2026-11-04 unnoticed: an e2e check expecting the old recall line format and a Windows-incompatible Unix permission assertion; both fixed.

hug's GitHub import maps each issue (open or closed) to a task with alias GH-<number>, keeps labels/assignees/milestone, turns checklists into acceptance items, and marks closed issues done / closed-as-not-planned dropped.
Hug scale ticket 44w1ev targets: every command and TUI interaction under 400 ms at 10,002 tasks; an unchanged board under 100 ms.
Muninn capture2 evaluation verdict: DO NOT SHIP; keep the existing shipping veto unless new evidence lifts it.
Late muninn memories were delivered via `jcode transcript --mode send` after the turn ended, so jcode submitted them as new user messages labelled `[transcription]`.
Revalidation of old memories is deferred to a later phase; muninn tidy covers only misplaced-memory moves for now.

Muninn open design topics parked: how personal vs shared memories are decided (new Engram memories without a project default to personal), imported data provenance (imports don't record client origin; jcode live-read vs import undecided), and the self-guiding CLI.
User rejected trimming recall for agent-to-agent messages, preferring a general redesign of recall for long messages (split into passages, rare-word keyword matching, explain-why-matched).
The muninn MCP self-guides: it sends session instructions and per-tool descriptions, so models find memory_forget without CLI help.
User wants to judge and tune muninn's capture algorithm with the foreman, so capture must record both what it saw and what it did (audit log).
Personal memories never go into the repo; only project memories are synced via .muninn/memories.jsonl.
hug's always-walk ruling means every command still walks the files, so the 100 ms target for an unchanged board is not met.
Hug workers commit only their own hunks (git add -p) and never others' uncommitted work, since multiple agents share the repo.
hug's MCP task_take requires `cwd` (kept optional in the schema, validated in build so the ticket's fix line shows) and detects branch/worktree from it.
Capture2 ship bar: durable recall up with CI excluding 0, precision/hallucination/trust inflation not worse, cost <= 2x baseline tokens; passing combos go to branch capture2 plus DM to coordinator.
hug's gitbranch network git calls all go through `runAt`, so a single hook point there (net.go) adds non-interactive deadlines to every network call.
muninn must keep wrong hits on the user's own messages from rising, since unrequested pushed memories are a cost to the user.
Board nudge latency p95: hug 27 ms (under 50 ms target), seid-lang 144 ms (over), mostly from humpback's package cache loading all 2,508 tasks.
User prefers reusing structures Muninn already builds (topic groups, similarity neighborhoods) over inventing new algorithms or keyword lists.
muninn scope: build locally, compile for every platform, support MCP, and offer both a web interface and a TUI.
In hug's board, the progress column is sized to the widest N/M among the board's tasks (about 6 columns typically), which shortens board titles by that width.
hug mem write lock: a waiter fails only if one holder keeps the lock 20 minutes; the error names the holder (pid, command, start time); a wait over 5 s prints who holds it.
muninn recall uses Ollama with nomic-embed-text embeddings; semantic scores are real (e.g. 0.57–0.66), not keyword-only.
huginn: project memories move to the same branch as tasks for easy sync and to avoid churn from multiple commits.
muninn v0.3.0-21 is installed live; the long-message recall redesign failed its test (relevant-hit share fell 62% to 47%) and stays on branch recall-passages.
muninn recall cutoffs (0.64, lowered to 0.58 for full-word matches) come from about a dozen test queries; a private 9-query check against real memories passes 9/9.
When a jcode memory is both read live and imported, both copies share one short id; recall shows it once from muninn's copy and forgetting removes both.
muninn project sharing: repos identified by first git commit; `muninn remember --project` and `muninn sync` write to .muninn/memories.jsonl; only project memories are exported, credentials held back.
User wants huginn easy to install: Homebrew formula and Scoop manifest in veridit/homebrew-tap, install.sh, and go install support.
hug's SQLite cache stores a ~6 MB blob rewritten inside each write transaction, growing the db from 15 to 22 MB at 10k tasks.

`hug task take` requires a model (`--model` or `HUG_MODEL`; `--model human` for a person) and exits 2 with a fix line if missing; the agent name is optional (`--as`, then `HUG_USER`, then jcode session name).
hug captures git's stderr, so GIT_TRACE output is swallowed; count git spawns with a logging git wrapper on PATH instead.
muninn tidy apply backs up memories.json first, applies only move decisions, and every move must be reversible with muninn rescope.

User wants the hug task section vocabulary validated by having several agents rewrite real tasks under different section names and a blind judge score which names keep the zoom-in section decision-relevant.
hug TUI: background reloads are deferred while a search, palette, confirm question, editor or grab is open, and applied once it closes.
hug CI runs tests without -v, so it is not visible whether the tmux test ran or was skipped on the runners.
hug's GitHub import is one-way: sending task status back to GitHub is not built.
muninn's capture proposed 7 notes on one session: 2 strengthened existing memories and 5 were new.
Hug worker protocol: the final report covers design, commits, replay numbers and open questions, and is also written to tmp/lanes/<ticket>.md.
hug TUI goldens are captured without SGR escapes, so they prove layout/padding changes but not colours; colours are covered by TestCodeQuietTint.
On Windows, hug's background syncer must start with a hidden console; without one, each git call opens a new console and passes crawl while holding the write lock.
hug TUI shows task ids bare (no brackets) in rows, detail header and trail; page focus in the trail is shown as '▸ ID'.

Jørgen's direction for hug recall nudges: the nudge replaces doctrine — say the right thing at the right moment, chosen by memory and semantics (the message and what the agent is about to do), not by a timer.

Jørgen's rule for hug: many agents writing at once is normal; every hug write must wait and then succeed, failing only after a wait far beyond any normal write, naming the lock holder, with a fix: line.
hug's TUI model exposes an `m.exec` seam that builds the editor Cmd, so tests can run it directly instead of going through tea.ExecProcess.
Production gaps noted: huginn unreleased and unused, muninn has no release tag since v0.3.0, personal/global memories never leave the Mac, and long-message recall is still noisy.
On the ~2,498-task seid board a full hug TUI refresh takes about 0.5 s, so loads must run off the UI thread; idle CPU was ~0.04 s over 15 s.
muninn memories have a `category` field (fact, preference, correction, entity, decision) that is messy in practice: 36 distinct values, most from imports.
Hug worker protocol: DM the coordinator (crab) before touching shared files and when a commit is releasable on its own; no desktop input and no Chrome.
The active row should be visibly marked all the way to the right (e.g. which agent is active on the current line), subtly.
User wants muninn to eventually own all memories: import jcode memories once, stop jcode background memory writing, and stop reading jcode files live, so forget/sync work on one source of truth.
House rule in this project: never rewrite files with Python scripts or `sed -i`; use the edit tool for every change.
huginn is pushed to a new private repo `veridit/huginn`; the shared git package `huginn/gitbranch` is public so muninn can import it (decision D14, reversible).
hug's MCP task_list goes through App.Execute's "ls" case, so cache changes to ls affect MCP output.
User decided the hug task description pattern should be established always and enforced so other agents adhere to it, via designed vocabulary and mechanism.
A duplicate entry in muninn's related-memories table broke recall and indexing on the live database; fixed in commit a0a50d3 after backing up the database.
Huginn TUI has golden screen tests (detail, markdown-warning, help, board) that must be regenerated and reviewed when screens change.
Recall outage was caused by duplicate neighbour edges from re-embedded dirty units; fixed by updating existing entries; live DB restored with 0 duplicate edges (commit a0a50d3).
hug MCP task_* tools build CLI argument lists passed through App.Execute, so CLI-level ref handling (e.g. stripping `task:`) covers MCP too.
In hug, writes must re-read under the write turn (costing one cached List) so a note cannot write from a pre-rebase snapshot.
Tagging hug tasks and memories by worktree (ticket x1t1t1) is still under discussion with Jørgen and must not be built yet.
hug's write path re-reads the board after taking the write lock, since the cached copy can be older than a background rebase; kept in Execute so reads don't pay for it.
Ticket jrj1vq is not built (still todo); main has only its offline scripts, so ez50rb adds `holds` as its own optional field rather than a field on jrj1vq.
hug's lint caches finding text, so changing finding wording requires bumping the cache version or old text keeps being served.
Hug worker protocol: if `hug task take` refuses because crab holds the task, run `hug task set <id> --assignee <name>` and say so.
User wants memory cleanup as a deliberate CLI command (e.g. `muninn tidy`), never automatic from hooks, recall, or agents' memory tools.
hug TUI test helper useEditor makes the test binary itself act as the editor, so tests avoid sh-script fake editors that fail on Windows.
No hug command adds an acceptance item; checks can be added via `hug task edit` with a non-interactive editor script.
muninn MCP server now scopes each jcode instance's MCP session to its own memories plus global ones (commit cf9f4db), and the installer writes --jcode-home into each mcp.json.
muninn capture proposed 619 memories overnight; 11 runs failed (6 provider errors, 4 timeouts, 1 unreadable reply) and are queued for retry.
In hug's TUI, every confirm prompt (all actionNames actions plus the tick prompt) must render in one prominent style (warning colour, bold or reverse) and read as a question.
Hug TUI key bindings: { and } step to the previous/next task, o/i/b/! switch view, and Space ticks only inside a task.
Scoop install path for muninn is untested (no Windows machine available); Windows/Linux model runs and fresh-machine `muninn install` download are also unverified.
hug mem forget accepts several ids or ids on stdin with --stdin, and checks every id first so one bad id forgets nothing.
hug TUI lazy-doc cache: findings come from the cache and task files are read only when a task is opened; at 10k tasks filter/move keystrokes take 53-127 ms.

Recall3 results: 6,094 replay rows, 4,406 blind labels, dense/RRF passes, 29 external arms over 100 questions; development long-precision +0.202 (95% CI [0.125, 0.265]); external ungated all-gold R@10 74/91 (CI [0.725, 0.890]).
`hug task lint` with findings must set `next:` to the fix command of the first finding (also in --json), not an unrelated task.
Hug lint: a "Depends on" line that is not a dependency gets its own finding code (suggested `not-a-dependency`), creates no Dependency, and does not block the task.
User wants muninn implemented for Claude Code, Codex, jcode, MCP and CLI.
Blind judge script for board nudge runs offline, redacts secrets, and uses the recall3 transport (DeepSeek Flash via jcode, no tools); it costs paid Flash calls.
In hug, the memory TUI goldens are fixed-width rows, so a shorter name shifts padding and goldens must be regenerated rather than hand-edited.
huginn: `next` supports filters such as `--type bug`, backed by a fixed `type:` field with a one-line description per type.
User decided huginn uses a disposable local SQLite cache synced from the markdown files on disk, rebuildable if deleted, for fast dependency/query operations.

muninn recall experiments (elephant) verdict: no ship — newer-memory weighting and model-rewritten search looked better on long messages but data was insufficient (2 messages from 1 session vs bar of 30 from 8); report at scratch/recall3/report.md.
In hug's TUI, keys never change meaning on hidden state: help lists R only while a newer hug exists.
In hug, capture's database writes must take the write turn around each short DB transaction, never across the model call; if the turn is held, a periodic capture skips rather than queues.
muninn recall latency is 110-180 ms warm and 420-650 ms after Ollama unloads the embedding model; at 16.6k units it was 0.86-1.9 s before optimisation.
User agreed groups and epics are independent views of the same tasks: list by group or by epic, and an epic can span several groups.

In hug, a slice-identity memo index must validate every hit and rebuild when stale, since callers may sort the slice in place; holding &tasks[0] keeps the old array alive so addresses can't be reused.
huginn task frontmatter records Branch and Worktree via `TakeAt`; `TakeAs` keeps its signature and delegates to an internal `transitionAt`.
Hug worker protocol: commit on main with a `Model: claude-opus-5-5` trailer, do not push, tag or run `hug task done`, and put CHANGELOG lines under `## Unreleased` at the top.
LongMemEval-S retrieval subset: official cohort is 91 positives; the earlier 94-positive diagnostics are superseded.
In hug, a not-found ref exits with code 2 and the message reads `not-found: <bare id>`.
Muninn's similarity neighborhoods are global across the whole corpus; topic groups are the existing per-client-unique grouping the user calls client groups.
Task-owned files live in a folder named by the task's id next to its file; the tool treats contents as plain files, with no special 'evidence' folder.
hug TUI `: sort` builder: empty values sort last in both directions, so the emptiness check happens before the direction flip.
muninn capture trial captured 724 memories since 10:00; jcode's own memory extraction had written nothing since the previous day at 10:24.

Hug worker protocol: test only the packages you changed, niced; never run the full suite (GitHub CI is the gate); never `ps -A`; stop and report any single test command running longer than 10 minutes.
The holds recall filter sits next to the records filter so it affects automatic recall only; `memory_search` still finds conditioned memories, and output is unchanged when no conditions are stored.
User decided huginn organizes tasks via folders as groups and links for dependencies; dependencies reference only the canonical short ID, never paths.
huginn cheap-model bar (D13): every command ends with a `next:` line, errors give the fixing command, one-command plain-flag actions, idempotent repeats, and at most ~10 MCP tools.
muninn recall cutoffs tuned on the user's 960 real memories: similarity ≥0.64 (≥0.58 if all query words appear), relative score ≥62% of best, max 5 memories, deduplicated per session.
huginn v0.1.1 is in brew; its MCP server is installed in all 6 jcode instances and `jcode mcp test huginn` lists its tools.
muninn/internal/holds parses three condition forms (until a date, while a task is open, while a branch is unmerged) and checks whether one has ended.
muninn background commands (capture, indexing, watcher, MCP server, sync) run at lower CPU priority and at most a quarter of cores; MUNINN_FULL_SPEED=1 disables the throttle.
hug's gitbranch Init keeps Head as a git call (once per sync); reading refs by hand (reftable, packed-refs) is considered risky.
hug's TUI Options gained a MainBranch field; vole's j2vwk0 adds fields nearby, and whoever lands second rebases.
hug's background sync burst test should key its push-count relaxation on the per-note interval versus the settle time, not on total elapsed time.
In hug's TUI, R exists only while a newer hug is installed (help lists it then); inside a prompt, palette or help, R is just a typed letter.
muninn has a `skip_records_above` setting that leaves 'record' memories out of automatic recall for long messages while `memory_search` still finds them; it is off by default.
Revalidation of old memories should only propose retiring false/stale memories, never rewrite them; original dates stay.
In hug, `note` spends most wall time off-CPU on two full syncs (open plus re-sync after write), each walking all files plus List cloning; git itself is only ~110 ms.
muninn's current recall threshold is 0.64, which lets 1 of 14 small-talk probes through while keeping 92% of real matches.
User prefers a self-guiding CLI (e.g. 'run muninn help for next step') over long written instructions, since cheap models call tools readily but skim rule paragraphs.
huginn tasks get a separate `origin` field (e.g. `backlog:STATBUS-093`); re-imports match on origin first, old IDs remain aliases, and lint flags duplicate origins.
Huginn TUI: opening a task scrolls just enough to keep the focused acceptance check in view at 80x24, rather than always going to the top.

2026-11-15: User decided the hug task model: three fixed levels only.
